subject: German

source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — German, Grade 6 (Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read directly from grade-6-curriculum-desings/GRADE-6-GERMAN-Curriculum-Designs.pdf via the Read tool (no pages param, per standing environment note). Essence statement: foreign language taught non-formally at Upper Primary alongside Arabic/French/Mandarin, targeting basic proficiency equivalent to A1 (Basic Language Level). Same 9-theme structure as Grade 6 French/Arabic (see curriculum-reference/grade-6/french.json, curriculum-reference/grade-6/arabic.json if present), informal 'du' register throughout (all example sentences use 'du', never formal 'Sie'). Time allocation: Listening and Speaking 27 lessons, Reading 18 lessons, Writing 9 lessons, +6 lessons showcasing (total 54+6).

subStrands.name: 1.1 Selective Listening, Imitative Speaking — Theme 1: Greetings and Introduction
specificLearningOutcomes: identify specific information from given texts
apply appropriate language structures in communication
appreciate the value of greetings in fostering respect
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you get all the needed information from a listening text?

linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili — greetings, self- and others' introduction
scopeNotes: model phrases: Das ist ___; Er/sie ist ___ Jahre alt

assessmentSignal: Listening rubric rewards correctly identifying general information from texts, imitating simulations appropriately, and correctly articulating/pronouncing words, with the top band explicitly rewarding an exerted effort to sound like a native speaker. Reading rubric rewards reading aloud with appropriate rhythm/stress/intonation/articulation and reading for comprehension by carrying out required tasks, with the top band rewarding native-speaker-like sound and exceeding the required comprehension tasks. Writing rubric (labelled 'for Reading' in the source but covering writing content) rewards correct punctuation and correct application of German orthography rules, with the top band rewarding correctly applying MORE than the given orthography rules.
notes: Grade 6 German has the same 9-theme, 3-strand (Listening and Speaking / Reading / Writing) shape as Grade 6 French/Arabic — the same 9 theme names (Greetings and Introduction, Family, My Surroundings, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Food and Drinks, My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around), informal 'du' register throughout (no formal 'Sie' register drilling). Numbers 20-100 taught cross-strand across Listening 1.2/Reading 2.2/Writing 3.2 (Family theme). Weather examples are Kenya-localized (Kisumu, Nyeri) even in German-language example sentences, matching the source PDF's own choice. To be built as web/src/skills/germanG6/ (9 themes x 3 strands: Speaking/Reading/Writing), following the exact frenchG6/arabicG6 file/strand/code pattern (strand ids g6-de-listening-speaking / g6-de-reading / g6-de-writing, codes LS.1-9 / R.1-9 / W.1-9).
